chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar, from Ḥammād, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

I asked him about a man who did not know whether he had prayed two rakʿahs or three. He said: He repeats. I said: Is it not said, “A faqih does not repeat the prayer”? So he said: That only applies to three and four. Thus it is understood as referring to the maghrib prayer or the morning prayer, because in these two prayers there is no sahw, and repeating is obligatory in them in every case.

key_terms.سَهْوَ: error or forgetful doubt in salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَقِيهٌ: a jurist; here, one who knows the proper legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone doubts whether they prayed two rakʿahs or three in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning doubt in the number of rakʿahs during salat (prayer). Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explains that the principle of not repeating the prayer applies to doubt between three and four, whereas doubt in maghrib or ghadah requires repeating the prayer because no sahw ruling applies in those two prayers.
